prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1138; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a rear-end collision at a low-speed intersection. The insured vehicle was struck from behind by a third-party vehicle, and the driver is named on the policy. Claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Police report obtained and reviewed. It confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of impact and records the other driver's account of the collision, which matches the scene description given at intake.

Entry 3: Photographs of the rear bumper and trunk area reviewed. Damage pattern is mostly in line with the described impact speed and direction. No prior damage to the vehicle is known from the file or from the prior claims search.

Entry 4: Two independent witnesses gave statements confirming the sequence of events as described by the insured and the other driver. Nothing in their accounts contradicts the reported facts.

Entry 5: Recorded statement taken from the claimant through counsel. Account of the accident and symptoms was consistent with the initial report. Claimant reports neck and back strain, and the injury profile fits the force of the crash. No prior injury to the same body areas is known.

Entry 6: Medical records received showing an initial evaluation followed by a usual course of physical therapy. Treatment tapered as the claimant improved, consistent with the expected recovery timeline for this type of soft tissue injury.

Entry 7: Coverage confirmed in force at the date of loss, with nothing suggesting the vehicle damage predates the policy period. File is progressing toward a settlement evaluation, with the claimant's account and treatment records consistent throughout.
